summary: Opt-in outbound read-only workstation agent, shared versioned protocol, FileService adapter, protected pairing state and six remote management commands.
decisions: Reuse existing FileService with writes disabled; validate each device, tool, root, arguments, deadline and bounded result independently of the gateway.
Interactive outbound HTTPS polling with reconnect backoff; no local listener, startup task, model call, elevated process or remote mutation capability.

Bind protected device credentials to the gateway, device and canonical enrolled folder. Store Windows credentials using current-user DPAPI through stdin; POSIX storage uses private directory/file modes.
Require explicit private dashboard origin for pairing; reject network/device roots, drive/home/credential roots and changed enrolled filesystem identity.
Serialize pairing/config updates, distinguish request expiry from device revocation and never replay a dispatched filesystem operation after reconnect.
Keep default local MCP and Codex launcher behavior; remote mode requires explicit setup, authenticated approval and foreground start.

limitations: No remote write/process activation or autostart service.
Stale owned state/run locks fail closed and require explicit inspection; no automatic lock stealing.
The local host is not an OS sandbox against a hostile same-user process or filesystem reparse races.
Human Google authorization, ChatGPT consent and hosted cross-platform qualification remain separate observations.
